_what_this_is: SECOND SOURCE — NOT the vindeklaration dataset. Every statement in data/wines.json comes from the declaration Systembolaget transcribes on that wine's own product page. Nothing in this file does. These records come from producers' e-labels and producers' own sites, gathered by hand-directed search, and they carry weaker and different provenance: the wine was matched to the source by a person's judgement, not by a product number.
_rules: src/build.py does not read this file and must not be changed to read it.
Never merge these records into data/wines.json, data/catalog.json or data/unknown.json.
If these declarations are ever shown on the site they need their own visual treatment and their own provenance line. That is the owner's decision, not this file's.
raw_ingredients, where present, is verbatim in the source language. Normalising it is src/normalize.py's job and it needs the original.
status 'not_found' means not found. It never means the producer published nothing — only that this run did not find it.
A record with robots_disallowed: true was fetched from a host whose robots.txt disallowed it. See _crawling for why, and CLAUDE.md for the decision.
_matching_rules_applied: producer matches, not a similar name or a sister estate
vintage matches exactly; a mismatch is a rejection, not an approximation
market matches; EU or Swedish language selection where one is offered
_crawling: Sequential, >= 0.6 s apart, project User-Agent from src/http.py, no retry loops. robots.txt is checked per host and honoured, with one exception decided 2026-07-30: an e-label page is fetched even where the host disallows crawling, because that page is the disclosure Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 requires and a blanket Disallow makes mandated consumer information unreadable to anyone comparing two bottles. The exception rests on not crawling — only URLs already discovered from the producer's own public linking, one request per wine, no traversal or enumeration — and does not extend to ordinary marketing sites. A technological measure (401, 403, 429, login wall, bot challenge) is absolute and stops the fetch. Records where the exception was used carry robots_disallowed: true.
batch: 2 — rendering reconnaissance: Domaine Billaud-Simon, Tommasi Viticoltori, Hain, Hällåkra Vingård, Vini Franchetti (27 wines, vintage 2024+, not_declared). The question was whether e-labels are readable at all or whether client-side rendering is universal, not how many declarations could be collected.

declarations.name: Tenuta Guado al Tasso Vermentino Bolgheri
declarations.evidence: Antinori's official shop 26generazioni.com carries one e-label link per product page ('Ingredienti e valori nutrizionali'). The only Guado al Tasso Vermentino Bolgheri in the shop's product sitemap is https://www.26generazioni.com/prodotto/vermentino-2025/, vintage 2025. No 2024 page exists in the sitemap. FETCHED 2026-07-30 UNDER THE ROBOTS EXCEPTION, AND STILL NOT READ. matu.st4.ch serves 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'; the page was fetched anyway as the disclosure Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 requires, one request, no traversal. The short link is a Scantrust QR redirect and answers 302 to https://elabel.scantrust.com/default/#/?uid=5430b284-2549-4692-aa38-7798c5d4c23b&api_key=<token>&qr=eA9Alxibv6ve . That destination returns an 828-byte HTML shell — title 'Scantrust', an empty <div id=app> and three JavaScript bundles — carrying no ingredient list, no nutrition table, no allergen line, no producer name and no vintage. The declaration is rendered client-side and this agent has no browser. The api_key is an issued token, not a URL parameter that can be reused: its prefix base64-decodes to {"campaign_id":35642} and its middle segment is a signer timestamp that incremented once per request across five sequential fetches, so it is minted per request and signed. Scantrust's documented e-label endpoint (GET /api/v2/products/{id}/elabel/) requires an account-issued UAT token on top of that. Under this project's rule that an issued token is a technological measure and absolute, no attempt was made to reach the data behind it, and no ingredient text is known for this wine.

_runs.batch: 2 — rendering reconnaissance across five producers in four countries (Billaud-Simon FR, Tommasi IT, Hain DE, Hällåkra SE, Vini Franchetti IT), 27 wines, all vintage 2024+ and not_declared
_runs.result: 27 attempted, 3 found, 23 not found, 1 rejected. VERDICT: server-rendered e-labels do exist. Weingut Hain's are plain HTML on the Winitas shop platform at {winery}.winitas-shop.de/elabel/{id}, with the ingredient list, nutrition table, allergens and Impressum in the server's response — no JavaScript, no token, no robots restriction. Client-side rendering is therefore not universal, contrary to the worry raised by Scantrust and IMERO. The dominant finding is nevertheless scarcity: four of the five producers publish no e-label and no ingredient list anywhere this run could see, so the binding constraint is that e-labels are rare and unlinked, not that they are unreadable.
